purpose: Follow-up on unresolved statement retrieval and false-positive source matches. Secondary statement copies are not treated as original contest evidence.

records.title: Muddy Hike
records.finding: A full text copy surfaced on a third-party homework Q&A site. It identifies the task as 'Problem F Muddy Hike' and includes the distinctive problem ID maps17.mu. The text describes a grid of nonnegative mud depths, a path from the leftmost to rightmost column using four-directional moves, and minimizing the maximum mud depth encountered. This is useful statement-content evidence and supports the MAPS17 naming association, but the host is not the contest organizer or an authoritative archive; no original MAPS 2017 package or official-hosted statement was retrieved. The task is a single minimax grid-path optimization problem, not a multi-stage operational scenario. Keep the depth assessment provisional and do not treat the copy as source approval.

sourceEvidence.observation: Full statement text includes Problem F Muddy Hike and problem ID maps17.mu; describes minimax mud-depth path across a grid.
Classifies muddyhike as a minimax path problem.

records.nextGate: Retrieve the official MAPS 2017 contest package or an authoritative Kattis source listing; inspect complete input/output and constraints before any final source or depth decision.

records.title: Grid
records.finding: The ICPC Kattis archive maps Grid / grid to Southeast USA 2015, Division 1. A separately retrieved Southeast USA 2015 Division 2 PDF contains a different digit-grid jump problem (move exactly the digit's number of cells; shortest path from top-left to bottom-right). That Division 2 statement is explicitly not accepted as evidence for this Division 1 candidate. No authoritative Division 1 statement was captured in this pass.

sourceEvidence.observation: Contains a distinct Division 2 Grid task; excluded as evidence for Division 1.

records.nextGate: Retrieve the official 2015 Southeast USA Division 1 problem package and verify the exact Grid problem before assessing depth.
